lessons.title: I'm hungry
lessons.canDo: Say you are hungry or thirsty
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Mia are in the kitchen after school.

items.note: Say 'I am hungry' when you want something to eat.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat rubbing his tummy and looking at an empty bowl in the kitchen

items.note: Say 'I am thirsty' when you want something to drink.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat holding an empty cup and looking thirsty

items.note: Use 'water' for the clear drink we have every day.

image.describe: a clear pitcher and glass filled with fresh water on a kitchen counter

items.note: Use 'bread' for a loaf or slices of baked bread.

image.describe: a warm golden loaf of bread with two slices on a wooden board

items.note: Say 'an apple' for one apple, and 'apples' for more than one.

image.describe: a shiny red apple with a green leaf

items.note: Use 'the' when you and the listener both know which thing you mean.

grammar.title: a, an, and the
grammar.explanation: Use 'an' before a word starting with a vowel sound like 'an apple'. Use 'the' when you point to one specific thing, like 'the apple' or 'the water'.

practice.prompt: Smarty rubs his tummy in the kitchen. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: Hungry means you want to eat.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Thirsty means you want something to drink.

practice.prompt: Match the words with their clues.
practice.explanation: Water is a drink, and bread and apple are foods.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence with the right word.
practice.explanation: Apple starts with a vowel sound, so use 'an apple'.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about the bread on the counter.
practice.explanation: Start with 'The' to talk about that specific bread.

practice.prompt: Sam is thirsty. Complete his sentence.
practice.explanation: Water is what you drink when you are thirsty.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: Use 'hungry' for food and 'thirsty' for a drink.

story.hook: What do Smarty and Mia find in the kitchen?

image.describe: A sunny kitchen where Mia the cat hands an apple and bread to Smarty the black cat, with a pitcher of water nearby.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Hi, Mia! I am hungry.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Hello, Smarty! I am thirsty.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Look! Water, bread, and two apples.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: The water is good. Thank you!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: And the apple is big! I am happy.

questions.prompt: How is Smarty at the start?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: I am hungry.

questions.prompt: How is Mia?
questions.explanation: Mia says: I am thirsty.

questions.prompt: What is big?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: And the apple is big!

mission.setup: You walk into Smarty's kitchen. Tell Smarty if you are hungry or thirsty.

turns.smarty: Hello! Are you hungry?
turns.hint: Say 'Yes, I am hungry' or 'No, I am thirsty'.

turns.smarty: I have water, bread, and an apple. What do you have?
turns.hint: Say 'I have water', 'I have bread', or 'I have an apple'.

lessons.title: Breakfast
lessons.scenario: Morning in the kitchen with Smarty and Sam.

items.note: Use 'breakfast' for the meal you have in the morning.

image.describe: a morning kitchen table set with bread, eggs, milk, and tea

items.note: Say 'an egg' for one, and 'eggs' when you have two or more.

image.describe: two white eggs in an egg cup on a breakfast plate

items.note: Use 'milk' for the white drink that cats love.

image.describe: a bottle and a small bowl of fresh white milk

items.note: Use 'tea' for the warm drink brewed from tea leaves.

image.describe: a steaming mug of amber tea on a saucer

items.note: Say 'for breakfast' to tell what you have at that meal.

practice.prompt: It is morning in the kitchen. Which meal is it?
practice.explanation: Breakfast is the meal we have in the morning.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for 'milk' at the end of the sentence.

practice.prompt: Match the breakfast items with their clues.
practice.explanation: Eggs, milk, and tea are common at breakfast.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence about the morning meal.
practice.text: I have bread and eggs ___ breakfast.
practice.explanation: Use 'for' before a meal name: for breakfast.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about Sam's father.
practice.explanation: Put the words in order: His father has tea.

practice.prompt: Smarty has one egg. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: After 'an', use the singular word 'egg'.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: I have eggs and milk for breakfast.
practice.answer: I have eggs and milk for breakfast.
practice.explanation: Great job naming your breakfast food and drink.

story.hook: What does Smarty have for breakfast?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat and Sam the cat having breakfast together in a bright kitchen with eggs, bread, milk, and tea.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Good morning, Smarty! Are you hungry?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Good morning, Sam! Yes, I am hungry.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I have two eggs and bread for breakfast.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: And tea?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Tea is for my mother. I have milk for you!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Milk! Thank you, Sam!

questions.prompt: What does Sam have for breakfast?
questions.explanation: Sam says: I have two eggs and bread for breakfast.

questions.prompt: Who has tea?
questions.explanation: Sam says: Tea is for my mother.

questions.prompt: What does Smarty get?
questions.explanation: Sam says: I have milk for you!

mission.setup: It is morning in Smarty's kitchen. Tell Smarty what you have for breakfast.

turns.smarty: Good morning! I have milk for breakfast. What do you have for breakfast?
accept: ^i have (?:an egg|eggs|bread|milk|tea|water|an apple)(?: and (?:an egg|eggs|bread|milk|tea|water|an apple))?(?: for breakfast)?$
turns.example: I have eggs and tea for breakfast.
turns.hint: Say 'I have eggs and tea' or 'I have bread and milk'.

turns.smarty: Do you have milk or tea? Say milk or tea!
turns.hint: Say 'I have milk' or 'I have tea'.

lessons.title: Do you like bananas?
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Ben check the snack basket in the kitchen.

items.note: Start a question with 'Do you like…?' to ask what someone enjoys.
Say 'I like…' when you enjoy a food or drink.
Say 'I do not like…' when you do not enjoy something.
Say 'a banana' for one, and 'bananas' when talking about them in general.

image.describe: two ripe yellow bananas side by side

items.note: Use 'cheese' without 'a' or 's' when talking about it in general.

image.describe: a yellow wedge of Swiss cheese with small holes

grammar.title: Do you like…? / I like / I do not like
grammar.explanation: Ask 'Do you like…?' and answer 'Yes, I like…' or 'No, I do not like…'. Use the plural for countable foods like 'bananas' and 'apples'.
examples: No, I do not like cheese.

practice.prompt: Which word names the long yellow fruit?
practice.explanation: A banana is a long yellow fruit.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Smarty asks a question starting with 'Do you like'.

practice.prompt: Match the phrases with their meanings.
practice.explanation: Use 'Do you like' to ask, 'I like' for yes, and 'I do not like' for no.

practice.prompt: Ask Ben about bananas. Complete the question.
practice.explanation: Questions about likes start with 'Do you like'.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence: say you do not enjoy tea.
practice.explanation: Put 'do not' before 'like' to make it negative.

practice.prompt: Ben loves cheese. Complete his answer.
practice.explanation: After 'Yes', use 'I like'.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: Use the plural 'bananas' when asking in general.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat and Ben the cat looking at a basket of bananas and a plate of cheese in the kitchen.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Smarty, do you like bananas?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: No, I do not like bananas.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Do you like cheese?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Yes! I like cheese and milk!

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I like bananas and cheese. We are happy!

questions.prompt: Smarty, do you like bananas?
questions.answer: No, I do not like bananas.
options: No, I do not like bananas.
questions.explanation: Smarty says: No, I do not like bananas.

questions.prompt: What does Smarty like?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: Yes! I like cheese and milk!

questions.prompt: Who likes bananas and cheese?
questions.explanation: Ben says: I like bananas and cheese.

mission.setup: Smarty wants to know what foods you like and do not like.

turns.smarty: Do you like bananas?
turns.hint: Say 'Yes, I like bananas' or 'No, I do not like bananas'.

turns.smarty: I like cheese! Do you like cheese?
turns.example: No, I do not like cheese.
turns.hint: Say 'Yes, I like cheese' or 'No, I do not like cheese'.

lessons.title: Review
lessons.scenario: Smarty, Mia, and Sam get breakfast ready in the kitchen.

practice.prompt: You want water or milk. How are you?
practice.explanation: Thirsty means you want something to drink.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.

practice.answer: I have eggs and bread for breakfast.

I have cheese and milk for breakfast.

lessons.title: Lunch and dinner
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Leo talk about midday and evening meals in the kitchen.

items.note: Use 'lunch' for the meal you have in the middle of the day.

image.describe: a midday meal with a steaming bowl of soup and bread

items.note: Use 'dinner' for the main meal you have in the evening.

image.describe: an evening dinner table with roast chicken and rice

items.note: Use 'rice' without 'a' or 's' when talking about it.

image.describe: a bowl of fluffy white steamed rice

items.note: Use 'soup' for warm liquid food you have in a bowl.

image.describe: a warm bowl of golden vegetable soup with a ladle

items.note: Use 'chicken' for the meat you have for lunch or dinner.

image.describe: a cooked golden chicken drumstick and breast on a dish

options: We have chicken and rice for dinner.
We have soup and bread for lunch.

practice.prompt: Match the words with their clues.
practice.explanation: Lunch is at midday, dinner is in the evening, and soup is a warm dish.

lessons.title: Can I have juice?
lessons.scenario: Ana visits Smarty in the kitchen for an afternoon snack.

items.note: Say 'Can I have…?' to ask for food or drink politely.
Use 'juice' for the sweet drink made from fruit.

image.describe: a tall glass of bright orange juice with a straw

items.note: Use 'cake' for a sweet baked treat.

image.describe: a slice of frosted layer cake on a small dessert dish

items.note: Say 'Of course!' as a friendly, polite way to say yes.
Say 'Here you are' when you hand something to someone.

grammar.title: Asking politely with Can I have…?
grammar.explanation: Use 'Can I have…, please?' to ask politely. Answer with 'Of course!' and 'Here you are!' when you give it.

practice.prompt: You want juice. How do you ask politely?
practice.explanation: Use 'Can I have…, please?' to ask for something politely.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: 'Of course! Here you are.' is a polite reply when giving food.

practice.prompt: Match the phrases with when you say them.
practice.explanation: Ask with 'Can I have', agree with 'Of course', and hand it over with 'Here you are'.

practice.prompt: Ana wants a slice of cake. Complete her polite request.
practice.explanation: Use 'Can I have' to ask for cake politely.

practice.prompt: Build the polite question for juice.
practice.explanation: Put the words in order: Can I have juice please?

practice.prompt: Say the polite reply aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: Say this warmly when you give someone food or drink.

lessons.title: Fruit and vegetables
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Zara unpack a basket of fresh produce in the kitchen.

items.note: Say 'an orange' for one, and 'oranges' for more than one.

image.describe: a bright round orange next to a halved orange slice

items.note: Notice the spelling for more than one: 'tomato' becomes 'tomatoes'.

image.describe: two ripe red tomatoes with green stems

items.note: Just like 'tomatoes', more than one 'potato' is spelled 'potatoes'.

image.describe: three brown potatoes sitting together on a kitchen counter

items.note: Say 'a carrot' for one, and 'carrots' for more than one.

image.describe: two fresh orange carrots with leafy green tops

items.note: Use 'fruit' as a group word for apples, bananas, and oranges.

grammar.title: Plurals: -s and -es
grammar.explanation: Add -s to most nouns (carrots, oranges), but add -es to words ending in -o like tomato -> tomatoes and potato -> potatoes.

practice.prompt: Apples, bananas, and oranges are all ___.
practice.explanation: Apples, bananas, and oranges are kinds of fruit.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.

I have three potatoes and two oranges.

practice.prompt: Match one with more than one.
practice.explanation: Tomato and potato add -es in the plural.

practice.explanation: Orange starts with a vowel sound, so use 'an orange'.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about the potatoes.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: Great job naming two fruits.

lessons.title: Delicious!
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Lily taste hot soup, cold juice, and sweet cake in the kitchen.

items.note: Say 'delicious' when food or drink tastes really good.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat smiling happily with stars around a steaming bowl of soup

items.note: Use 'hot' for food or drinks that are very warm, like fresh tea or soup.

image.describe: a steaming mug of hot tea with rising heat lines

items.note: Use 'cold' for chilled drinks or food from the fridge.

image.describe: a frosty glass of cold water with ice cubes and droplets

items.note: Use 'sweet' for sugary foods and ripe fruit like cake and bananas.

image.describe: a slice of sweet strawberry cake with cherries on top

items.example: The soup is hot, but the juice is cold.
items.note: Use 'but' to join two different or opposite ideas.

practice.prompt: The chicken soup tastes amazing! Which word fits?

practice.explanation: Listen for the contrast: hot tea, but cold juice.

practice.prompt: Match the food or drink with how it usually is.
practice.explanation: Soup is hot, ice water is cold, and cake is sweet.

practice.prompt: Join the two opposite ideas with one word.

practice.explanation: Use 'but' to connect two contrasting ideas.

practice.explanation: Put the words in order: The cake is sweet and delicious.

practice.answer: The soup is hot and delicious!
practice.explanation: Great job describing the soup.

lessons.title: Some and any
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Mia set the kitchen table with plates, cups, and glasses.

items.note: Use 'some' in positive sentences and polite requests when you do not give an exact number.

items.example: We do not have any milk.
items.note: Use 'any' in negative sentences and questions like 'Do you have any…?'.
Use 'plate' for the flat dish you put food on.

image.describe: a clean round white dinner plate

items.note: Use 'cup' for a mug with a handle, often for hot drinks like tea.

image.describe: a ceramic teacup with a handle

items.note: Use 'glass' for I am thirsty.ing glass; more than one is 'glasses'.

image.describe: a clear empty drinking glass on a counter

grammar.title: some and any
grammar.explanation: Use 'some' when you have something or ask politely ('I have some rice', 'Can I have some water?'). Use 'any' with 'not' and in 'Do you have…?' questions ('We do not have any milk', 'Do you have any eggs?').
examples: We do not have any cheese.

practice.explanation: Use 'some' in positive sentences when you do not count the exact amount.

practice.answer: We do not have any milk.
options: We do not have any milk.
practice.explanation: In negative sentences with 'not', use 'any'.

practice.prompt: Match each item with what it is for.
practice.explanation: Food goes on a plate, hot tea in a cup, and cold drinks in a glass.

practice.prompt: Ask Smarty if he has cheese. Complete the question.

story.hook: What do Smarty and Mia have, and what is missing?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat and Mia the cat setting plates, cups, and glasses on the kitchen table with bread and water.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Smarty, we have two plates, two cups, and two glasses.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Good! We have some bread and some rice.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Do we have any juice?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: No, we do not have any juice, but we have some cold water.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Can I have a glass and some water, please?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Of course! Here you are.

questions.prompt: What do Smarty and Mia NOT have?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: No, we do not have any juice.

questions.prompt: What does Mia ask for?
questions.explanation: Mia says: Can I have a glass and some water, please?

mission.setup: Help Smarty check what is in the kitchen using 'some' and 'any'.

turns.smarty: I have a plate, a cup, and a glass. Ask me politely for some water or juice!
turns.example: Can I have some water, please?
turns.hint: Say 'Can I have some water, please?' or 'Can I have some juice, please?'.

turns.smarty: Here you are! Do we have any cake?
turns.example: No, we do not have any cake.
turns.hint: Say 'Yes, we have some cake' or 'No, we do not have any cake'.

lessons.title: Feed Smarty
lessons.canDo: Offer food and say you are full
lessons.scenario: A big dinner party in Smarty's kitchen with fish, sandwiches, and treats.

items.note: Use 'fish' for both one fish and fish as food.

image.describe: a cooked fish served with lemon slices on a dinner plate

items.note: Say 'a sandwich' for one, and 'sandwiches' for more than one.

image.describe: a fresh sandwich made with bread, cheese, and tomato slices

items.note: Say 'I am full' when you have had enough food and cannot eat more.

practice.prompt: What is Smarty the cat's favorite dinner?
practice.explanation: Cats love fish! Smarty likes fish.

options: Can I have a cheese sandwich, please?
Can I have fish and rice, please?

practice.prompt: Match the phrases with their meanings.

story.hook: Does Smarty finish all the food at dinner?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat sitting happily at a kitchen table full of fish, sandwiches, soup, fruit, and cake with Mia and Sam.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Good evening, Smarty! Do you like fish?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Yes! I like fish! Can I have some fish, please?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Of course! Here you are. And a chicken sandwich!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: The fish is delicious! And the sandwich is good!

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Do you have any cake?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: No, thank you! I am full!

questions.prompt: What does Smarty ask for?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: Can I have some fish, please?

questions.prompt: What sandwich does Sam give Smarty?
questions.explanation: Sam says: And a chicken sandwich!

questions.prompt: Why does Smarty say no to cake?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: No, thank you! I am full!

mission.setup: Join Smarty's kitchen feast! Ask for food, say how it tastes, and say when you are full.

turns.smarty: Welcome to dinner! We have fish, chicken, rice, and sandwiches. What do you want?
turns.example: Can I have some fish, please?
turns.hint: Ask politely: 'Can I have some fish, please?' or 'Can I have a sandwich, please?'.

turns.smarty: Of course! Here you are. Is it good?
accept: ^(?:yes )?(?:it is |the fish is |the sandwich is )?(?:delicious|good|hot and delicious)$
turns.hint: Say 'Yes, it is delicious!' or 'It is good!'.

turns.smarty: Do you have any cake or fruit, or are you full?
accept: ^(?:no thank you )?i am full(?: thank you)?$
turns.example: No, thank you! I am full!
turns.hint: Say 'No, thank you! I am full!' or ask for cake or fruit.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Good evening, friends! I am hungry!

panels.text: Hello, Smarty! We have tomatoes, potatoes, and carrots.

panels.text: And I have fish and rice for dinner!

panels.text: Fish! I like fish! Can I have a big plate, please?

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: Of course! Here you are. The soup is hot, but the juice is cold.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: The fish is delicious! And the sweet cake is good!

panels.speaker: Sam
panels.text: Do you have any cheese, Smarty?

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: No, we do not have any cheese. And I am full! Good night—wait! Who is at the door?
